text: An expression of energy density is given by $u=\frac{α}{β}\sin \left (\frac{αx}{kt}\right )$, where $α,β$ are constants, $x$ is displacement, $k$ is Boltzmann constant and t is the temperature. The dimensions of $β$ will be :
sourceReference: NTA JEE Main JEE Main 2022 (Online) 27th July Evening Shift via ExamSIDE (questions.examside.com)

solution.body:
The argument of a sine is dimensionless, so $\left [\dfrac{αx}{kt}\right ]=[\mathrm{M}^{0}\mathrm{L}^{0}\mathrm{T}^{0}]$, giving

$[α]=\dfrac{[kt]}{[x]}$

Here $kt$ ($k$ in $\text{J K}^{-1}$ times a temperature in K) has the dimensions of energy, $[\mathrm{ML}^{2}\mathrm{T}^{-2}]$, and $[x]=[\mathrm{L}]$:

$[α]=\dfrac{[\mathrm{ML}^{2}\mathrm{T}^{-2}]}{[\mathrm{L}]}=[\mathrm{MLT}^{-2}]$

The sine factor is dimensionless, so $[u]=\dfrac{[α]}{[β]}$, where $u$ is energy per unit volume, $[u]=[\mathrm{ML}^{-1}\mathrm{T}^{-2}]$:

$[β]=\dfrac{[α]}{[u]}=\dfrac{[\mathrm{MLT}^{-2}]}{[\mathrm{ML}^{-1}\mathrm{T}^{-2}]}=[\mathrm{M}^{0}\mathrm{L}^{2}\mathrm{T}^{0}]$

Hence, the correct option is (D).
sourceReferences: ExamSIDE explanation for JEE Main 2022 (Online) 27th July Evening Shift

text:
A body of mass $10\mathrm{kg}$ is projected at an angle of $45^{\circ }$ with the horizontal. The trajectory of the body is observed to pass through a point $(20,10)$. If $\mathrm{T}$ is the time of flight, then its momentum vector, at time $\mathrm{t}=\frac{\mathrm{T}}{\sqrt{2}}$, is $_____________$.

[Take $\mathrm{g}=10\mathrm{m}/\mathrm{s}^{2}$ ]
sourceReference: NTA JEE Main JEE Main 2022 (Online) 27th July Evening Shift via ExamSIDE (questions.examside.com)

solution.body:
For projection at $45^{\circ }$ with horizontal range $R$, the trajectory is $y=x\tan 45^{\circ }\left (1-\dfrac{x}{R}\right )$. It passes through $(20,10)$:

$10=20\left (1-\frac{20}{R}\right )\Rightarrow R=40\text{m}$

$R=\frac{u^{2}\sin 90^{\circ }}{g}\Rightarrow u^{2}=40\times 10=400\Rightarrow u=20\text{m s}^{-1}$

The time of flight is

$T=\frac{2u\sin 45^{\circ }}{g}=\frac{2\times 20\times \frac{1}{\sqrt{2}}}{10}=2\sqrt{2}\text{s},t=\frac{T}{\sqrt{2}}=2\text{s}$

At $t=2\text{s}$: $v_{x}=u\cos 45^{\circ }=10\sqrt{2}\text{m s}^{-1}$ and $v_{y}=u\sin 45^{\circ }-gt=(10\sqrt{2}-20)\text{m s}^{-1}$.

$⃗{p}=m⃗{v}=10\left [10\sqrt{2}\hat{i}+(10\sqrt{2}-20)\hat{j}\right ]=100\sqrt{2}\hat{i}+(100\sqrt{2}-200)\hat{j}$

Hence, the correct option is (D).
sourceReferences: ExamSIDE explanation for JEE Main 2022 (Online) 27th July Evening Shift

text:
With reference to the observations in photo-electric effect, identify the correct statements from below :

(A) The square of maximum velocity of photoelectrons varies linearly with frequency of incident light.

(B) The value of saturation current increases on moving the source of light away from the metal surface.

(C) The maximum kinetic energy of photo-electrons decreases on decreasing the power of LED (light emitting diode) source of light.

(D) The immediate emission of photo-electrons out of metal surface can not be explained by particle nature of light/electromagnetic waves.

(E) Existence of threshold wavelength can not be explained by wave nature of light/ electromagnetic waves.

Choose the correct answer from the options given below :
sourceReference: NTA JEE Main JEE Main 2022 (Online) 27th July Evening Shift via ExamSIDE (questions.examside.com)

solution.body:
Statement (A): from $\dfrac{1}{2}mv_{\max }^{2}=hν-𝜙$, $v_{\max }^{2}=\dfrac{2h}{m}ν-\dfrac{2𝜙}{m}$, which is linear in $ν$. Correct.

Statement (B): moving the source away lowers the intensity at the surface, so fewer photoelectrons are emitted and the saturation current decreases. Incorrect.

Statement (C): the maximum kinetic energy depends only on the frequency of the light and the work function, not on the power of the source. Incorrect.

Statement (D): each photon gives its whole energy to one electron at once, so the particle nature of light explains immediate emission. Incorrect.

Statement (E): on the wave picture, light of any wavelength would eject electrons if intense enough, so a threshold wavelength cannot be explained; it needs the photon picture, $\dfrac{hc}{λ_{0}}=𝜙$. Correct.

Only statements (A) and (E) are correct.

Hence, the correct option is (B).
sourceReferences: ExamSIDE explanation for JEE Main 2022 (Online) 27th July Evening Shift

text: A wire of length 30 cm, stretched between rigid supports, has it$'s n^{th}$ and $(n + 1)^{th}$ harmonics at 400 Hz and 450 Hz, respectively. If tension in the string is 2700 N, it's linear mass density is $____________ kg/m$.
sourceReference: NTA JEE Main JEE Main 2022 (Online) 27th July Evening Shift via ExamSIDE (questions.examside.com)

solution.body:
For a string fixed at both ends, consecutive harmonics differ by the fundamental frequency:

$f_{1}=450-400=50\text{Hz}$

With $L=30\text{cm}=0.30\text{m}$ and $f_{1}=\dfrac{v}{2L}$:

$v=2Lf_{1}=2\times 0.30\times 50=30\text{m s}^{-1}$

The speed of a transverse wave on a stretched string is $v=\sqrt{\dfrac{T}{μ}}$, so

$μ=\frac{T}{v^{2}}=\frac{2700}{(30)^{2}}=3\text{kg m}^{-1}$

Hence, the answer is 3.
sourceReferences: ExamSIDE explanation for JEE Main 2022 (Online) 27th July Evening Shift

text:
A solid cylinder is suspended symmetrically through two massless strings, as shown in the figure. The distance from the initial rest position, the cylinder should be unbinding the strings to achieve a speed of $4\mathrm{ms}^{-1}$, is $____________ cm. ($take g = $10\mathrm{ms}^{-2}$)


[IMG]
sourceReference: NTA JEE Main JEE Main 2022 (Online) 27th July Evening Shift via ExamSIDE (questions.examside.com)

solution.body:
As the strings unwind, the cylinder falls with $v=ωr$, where $r$ is its radius. The strings do no work, because the points of the cylinder touching them are momentarily at rest, so mechanical energy is conserved.

For a solid cylinder $I=\dfrac{1}{2}mr^{2}$, so after falling a height $h$ from rest:

$mgh=\dfrac{1}{2}mv^{2}+\dfrac{1}{2}\left (\dfrac{1}{2}mr^{2}\right )\dfrac{v^{2}}{r^{2}}=\dfrac{3}{4}mv^{2}$

The mass and radius cancel:

$h=\dfrac{3v^{2}}{4g}=\dfrac{3\times 16}{4\times 10}=1.2\text{m}=120\text{cm}$

Hence, the answer is 120.
sourceReferences: ExamSIDE explanation for JEE Main 2022 (Online) 27th July Evening Shift
